name: SM-130686
lead: SM-130686 is an experimental, orally active, non-peptide growth hormone secretagogue built on an oxindole scaffold. It was characterised in the early 2000s as a ghrelin receptor agonist that stimulates growth hormone release.[1][2][3]

Published work consists of medicinal chemistry, laboratory pharmacology, animal studies and analytical methods for doping control. No human efficacy trials were found, and the compound is not an approved medicine.[1][4][5]
infobox: Non-peptide growth hormone secretagogue (ghrelin receptor agonist)
EC50 about 3.0 nM in rat pituitary cells[1]

paras: The active form is the (+)-enantiomer, described as (+)-6-carbamoyl-3-(2-chlorophenyl)-(2-diethylaminoethyl)-4-trifluoromethyloxindole; the other enantiomer showed reduced activity, and the absolute configuration was confirmed by X-ray crystallography.[1] A 2009 chemistry paper reported a catalytic enantioselective synthesis route to the compound.[6] Follow-up structure-activity work produced analogues with much higher binding affinity, one of which was reported to produce body-weight gain in rats when given orally.[7]

SM-130686 acts as an agonist at the ghrelin (growth hormone secretagogue) receptor.[7] Receptor-mapping work has examined where small-molecule agonists and the natural ligand bind on that receptor.[3] In cultured rat pituitary cells the compound stimulated growth hormone release, and the original paper reported a good pharmacokinetic profile in animals.[1] Separate papers describe its pharmacological profile as a new orally active secretagogue.[4][8]
A 2006 study described a method for detecting growth hormone secretagogue therapeutics, in the context of doping control, in human urine.[5]
No studies found. Published work on SM-130686 is limited to chemistry, cell-based assays, animal research and analytical methods.[1][4][5][7]

timeline.event: Oxindole growth hormone secretagogues, including SM-130686, reported in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry and the Journal of Endocrinology.[1][4]
Doping-control urine method for secretagogues published.[5]

card.summary: An experimental oral oxindole growth hormone secretagogue known from lab and animal papers, with no human trials of muscle or appearance effects.
card.note: Not an approved medicine; no human efficacy or safety trials were found.

quick.overview:
SM-130686 is a research compound that stimulates growth hormone release by activating the ghrelin receptor. Unlike peptide secretagogues it is a small molecule designed to work by mouth.

The literature is mostly chemistry and animal or cell-based pharmacology from the 2000s. No human trials were found.
quick.mechanism: It binds and activates the ghrelin (growth hormone secretagogue) receptor, which triggers growth hormone release from pituitary cells in laboratory studies.
quick.risks: Human safety has not been published. The compound is experimental, and analytical methods exist for detecting secretagogues in urine for doping control.
